correctness.rationale: On K(n,2), closed-neighborhood condition is Cij=W−si−sj+2fij≥1. Summing all vertices forces integer W≥2 for n≥12. Summing over pairs incident with a fixed point gives (n−3)W−(n−4)si≥n−1, whence W=2 forces each integer si≤0, impossible as Σsi=4; so W≥3. For odd n, the already-known Hamiltonian-cycle-on-small-part construction has W=3. For even n=2a+2, cross pairs −1, within pairs +1, a Hamiltonian X-cycle and three disjoint Y edges upgraded to +2 give W=4, row sums sx=−1 and sy=1 or 2, all closed sums ≥1, and every negative edge is disjoint from a +2 X-cycle edge. Independently reconstructed the functions and verified all conditions at each n=12..24. The universal proof handles all n≥12; exact even minimum (3 or 4) remains unresolved.
